chains.title: GABPA/ETS gain-of-binding at the TERT promoter C250T allele

links.claim: The alt A allele strengthens GABPA binding: GABPA is an own-model ETS factor in QBiC group G003 with the group alt-more sign (z 71.32), GABPA ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain this site, and ETS factors are reported to bind mutant TERT promoters; GABPA was chosen over ETV5 because GABPA has ChIP evidence at this site while ETV5 does not.
The variant lies within the TERT promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 (PLS), a promoter element.
TERT is the nearest protein-coding gene, 0.0 kb from its TSS and upstream on the minus strand.
GABPA is expressed in the glioblastoma DepMap subtype context at 15.52 TPM; the available GABPA ChIP peaks are from HepG2 and SK-N-SH, not glioblastoma.

If GABPA binding at the alt allele raises TERT, this would fit the general association of TERT promoter mutations with telomerase activation in glioblastoma and melanoma; direct allele-specific TERT expression evidence is not provided.

predictions: Allele-specific GABPA ChIP-qPCR should show higher GABPA occupancy on the alt allele than on the ref allele in a C250T-heterozygous tumor cell line.
GABPA knockdown or CRISPR should reduce TERT expression preferentially in C250T-heterozygous glioblastoma/melanoma cells.
Mutating the ETS motif or blocking GABPA should reduce alt-allele-dependent TERT reporter activity.
falsified_if: Allele-specific GABPA ChIP or footprinting shows no difference between alt and ref at chr5:1295135 in relevant tumor cells.
GABPA knockdown/CRISPR in a C250T-heterozygous glioblastoma or melanoma line does not reduce TERT expression.

chains.title: No direct TF-mediated allelic effect
predictions: There should be no allele-specific TF binding at chr5:1295135 after controlling for linked variants.
TERT expression should not differ by this allele once linked causal variants in cis are accounted for.
The recurrent C250T observation should be explainable as a mutational hotspot/passenger marker or as a linked-variant signal rather than a direct TF-mediated effect.
falsified_if: Allele-specific GABPA/ETS occupancy at chr5:1295135 and allele-specific TERT expression persist after controlling for linked variants such as rs2853669 in cis.

chains.title: ETV5/ETS gain-of-binding at the TERT promoter C250T allele

links.claim: The alt A allele binds ETV5 more strongly in QBiC-SELEX: ETV5 is the best own-model ETS model in group G003 (z 167.5, effect 2.421, alt more), but no ENCODE ETV5 ChIP-seq peak contains this site.
The variant lies within the TERT promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 (PLS).
TERT is the nearest protein-coding gene, 0.0 kb from its TSS.
ETV5 is expressed in the glioblastoma DepMap subtype context at 22.15 TPM.
If ETV5 is the relevant ETS factor, the alt allele should increase TERT expression/telomerase activity, fitting the general TERT promoter mutation association; this is not directly tested here.

predictions: ETV5 ChIP-qPCR should show higher ETV5 occupancy on the alt allele than on the ref allele in relevant tumor cells.
ETV5 knockdown should reduce TERT expression preferentially in C250T-heterozygous cells.
The ETV5 motif model should outperform GABPA and other ETS models in allele-specific reporter assays.
falsified_if: ETV5 does not occupy this site allele-specifically in relevant tumor cells.
ETV5 perturbation does not affect TERT expression in C250T-heterozygous cells.

chains.title: MBD1 repressor-loss at the TERT promoter C250T allele

links.claim: The ref G allele binds MBD1 more strongly than the alt A allele in QBiC-SELEX (MBD1 own model z -41.31, effect -1.236).
The variant lies within the TERT promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 (PLS).
TERT is the nearest protein-coding gene, 0.0 kb from its TSS.
MBD1 is expressed in the glioblastoma DepMap subtype context at 31.48 TPM.
If MBD1 represses TERT, loss of MBD1 binding on the alt allele would de-repress TERT; no cited evidence establishes MBD1 occupancy at TERT or MBD1-dependent TERT repression.

predictions: MBD1 ChIP-qPCR should show stronger MBD1 occupancy on the ref allele than on the alt allele.
MBD1 knockdown should increase TERT expression, mimicking the alt allele if MBD1 is a repressor.
The alt allele should increase TERT reporter activity through loss of MBD1 repression, not ETS activation.
falsified_if: MBD1 does not occupy this site or does not show stronger ref-allele binding.
MBD1 knockdown does not increase TERT expression, or MBD1 is not a TERT repressor.

grades_v0.reason: E06 shows GABPA as an own-model ETS member of group G003 with an alt-more group sign (GABPA z 71.32), but this is QBiC-SELEX in vitro binding only. No allele-specific ChIP, MPRA, reporter, or perturbation evidence is cited. Also, GABPA is not the group’s best model; ETV5 is, and H1 gives no independent reason to choose GABPA over ETV5 or other ETS factors.
E03 directly places the variant inside cCRE EH38E3622530, a PLS promoter-like element; E01 also annotates a promoter regulatory feature at this site.
E02 directly reports TERT as 0.0 kb from its TSS, upstream on the minus strand; E01 also assigns an upstream TERT transcript consequence.
E06, with E05 defining the DepMap Glioblastoma subtype context, lists GABPA as own-model covered at 15.52 TPM.

E04a/E04d/E04g/E04h support that TERT promoter mutations are common in glioblastoma/melanoma and broadly associated with telomerase activation, but they do not show that C250T itself raises TERT expression in an allele-specific manner. The higher-TERT prediction is inferential, not directly tested.

E06 shows ETV5 as the best own-model ETS model in G003 (z 167.5, effect 2.421, alt binds more) with all passing group models sharing that sign. This is strong QBiC-SELEX support but still only an in vitro binding prediction, not allele-specific occupancy or a functional assay.
E03 directly places the variant in the TERT promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 (PLS); E01 annotates a promoter regulatory feature.
E02 directly reports TERT as the nearest protein-coding gene at 0.0 kb from its TSS, upstream on the minus strand.
E06 lists ETV5 as own-model covered at 22.15 TPM in the defined DepMap Glioblastoma subtype context.

E04a/E04d/E04h support a general TERT promoter mutation–telomerase association in glioblastoma/melanoma, but there is no ETV5-specific or C250T allele-specific expression evidence showing that ETV5 binding raises TERT.

E09 shows MBD1 as an own-model factor with z -41.31 and effect -1.236, meaning the ref G allele binds more than the alt A allele. This is QBiC-SELEX in vitro binding only; no allele-specific occupancy or functional assay is cited.
E03 directly places the variant in the TERT promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 (PLS); E01 annotates a promoter regulatory feature.
E02 directly reports TERT as 0.0 kb from its TSS, upstream on the minus strand.
E09 lists MBD1 as own-model covered at 31.48 TPM in the defined DepMap Glioblastoma subtype context.

The phenotype claim depends on MBD1 repressing the TERT promoter and loss of MBD1 de-repressing TERT, but no cited evidence shows MBD1 represses TERT. E09 only shows predicted differential binding, and E04a/E04d only give a general TERT promoter mutation–telomerase association.

grades_final.reason: QBiC-SELEX gives GABPA an own-model alt-more signal in G003 (z 71.32), but this is an in vitro binding prediction. E16 shows GABPA ChIP peaks containing the site only in HepG2/SK-N-SH and does not show allele-specific binding or glioblastoma occupancy. E18a supports ETS factors generally binding mutant TERT promoters, not GABPA at this site.
E03 directly places the variant in cCRE EH38E3622530, a promoter-like PLS element, and E01 annotates a promoter regulatory feature at the site.
E02 reports TERT at 0.0 kb from the TSS, upstream on the minus strand, and E01 annotates a TERT upstream_gene_variant consequence.
E06 reports GABPA expression at 15.52 TPM in the DepMap glioblastoma subtype context, and E16 confirms the available GABPA ChIP peaks are from HepG2 and SK-N-SH, not glioblastoma.

E04a/E04d/E04g/E04h support the general association of TERT promoter mutations, including C250T, with telomerase activation and glioblastoma, and E18a supports ETS involvement generally. But none directly shows GABPA-mediated or allele-specific TERT expression at C250T.

E06 provides QBiC-SELEX evidence that ETV5 is the best own-model ETS model in G003 with alt-more binding (z 167.5, effect 2.421), but QBiC-SELEX alone is at most weak support for a cellular binding link. E17 only reports absence of ETV5 ChIP peaks, which does not support occupancy.
E03 directly places the variant in the TERT promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 (PLS), and E01 annotates a promoter regulatory feature at the site.
E02 reports TERT at 0.0 kb from its TSS, and E01 annotates the variant as a TERT upstream_gene_variant.
E06 reports ETV5 expression at 22.15 TPM in the DepMap glioblastoma subtype context.
E04a/E04d/E04h support the general association of TERT promoter mutations with telomerase activation and disease, but the chain provides no ETV5-specific or allele-specific TERT expression evidence.

E09 provides only QBiC-SELEX evidence that MBD1 binds the ref allele more strongly (z -41.31, effect -1.236). This is an in vitro binding prediction and does not establish MBD1 occupancy at the TERT promoter in cells.
E03 directly places the variant in the TERT promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 (PLS), and E01 annotates a promoter regulatory feature at the site.
E02 reports TERT at 0.0 kb from its TSS, and E01 annotates the variant as a TERT upstream_gene_variant.

The phenotype link has no cited evidence: nothing establishes MBD1 occupancy at TERT, MBD1-dependent TERT repression, or de-repression of TERT by loss of MBD1 binding at the alt allele.

checks.why: Tests whether GABPA actually occupies this element in a glioblastoma biosample, which would upgrade or falsify the QBiC-SELEX-only binding link and help distinguish H1 from H2.
Directly compares ETV5 occupancy at the variant against GABPA and tests whether the strongest QBiC-SELEX model corresponds to real binding in the relevant cell type.
The H3 phenotype requires evidence that MBD1 represses TERT; a targeted literature search would determine whether the repressor-loss mechanism has any experimental support or should be dropped.

A major molecular feature of melanoma is abnormal telomerase activation; this is most often caused by telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter mutations, which occur in 50-82% of cases and are the most common noncoding alteration in this cancer.
Understanding both telomere-dependent and -independent TERT functions is essential for developing effective biomarkers and therapies that overcome resistance and slow melanoma progression.
CDKN2A and CDK4 mutations act through UV-dependent and cell cycle disruption pathways, while BAP1, POT1, and TERT mutations are considered UV-independent.
Mutations in the telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter region (TPM), particularly C228T and C250T, are common in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma (GBM).

The rs2853669 C allele may increase GBM susceptibility and, when in cis with TPM, is associated with reduced TERT expression and poorer prognosis, underscoring its biological and clinical significance in TPM-mutant GBM.
Additionally, loss of either USP10 or FOXM1 suppresses the expression of the downstream target Telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT), triggering cellular senescence.

TERT promoter (TERTp) mutations are among the most frequent molecular alterations in isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) wild-type glioblastoma (GBM), yet the molecular profiles and prognostic implications associated with TERTp status remain incompletely characterized.
Among 112 patients, 70 (62.5%) harbored TERTp mutations.
